assessment.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Bab al-Mandabu se prudce vyhrotila poté, co saúdsky podporované vládní síly zahájily rozsáhlou ofenzívu proti Hútíům. V odvetě hnutí Hútí provádí raketové a dronové útoky na saúdská letiště a ropná zařízení Aramco, což zvyšuje riziko přímého regionálního konfliktu a ohrožuje svobodu plavby.
assessment.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab strait has escalated sharply after Saudi-backed government forces launched a major offensive against the Houthis. In retaliation, the Houthi movement is launching missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and Aramco oil facilities, heightening the risk of direct regional conflict and threatening freedom of navigation.

recommendations.reason_cs: Přestože vládní síly zajišťují část vodní cesty, hrozby Hútíů vůči leteckému i námořnímu provozu udržují vysoké geopolitické riziko a nutnost objížděk. Akcie zůstávají pod tlakem vysokých nákladů na pojištění a delších tras.
recommendations.reason_en: Although government forces are securing parts of the waterway, Houthi threats to air and maritime traffic maintain high geopolitical risk and the need for detours. Stocks remain under pressure from high insurance costs and longer routes.

recommendations.sector_cs: Obranný průmysl (např. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)
recommendations.sector_en: Defense Industry (e.g. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)
recommendations.reason_cs: Intenzivní útoky drony a balistickými raketami na saúdská letiště a infrastrukturu vedou k růstu poptávky po systémech protivzdušné obrany. Tento sektor těží z eskalace napětí na Blízkém východě.
recommendations.reason_en: Intensive drone and ballistic missile attacks on Saudi airports and infrastructure are driving up demand for air defense systems. This sector benefits directly from the escalation of tension in the Middle East.

recommendations.sector_cs: Ropa a Plyn (např. Shell, BP, Chevron)
recommendations.reason_cs: Přímé útoky na zařízení společnosti Saudi Aramco a nestabilita v oblasti Rudého moře vytvářejí rizikovou přirážku na cenách ropy. To podporuje marže a tržby globálních energetických gigantů.
recommendations.reason_en: Direct attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and instability in the Red Sea create a risk premium on oil prices. This supports margins and revenues for global energy giants.

recommendations.sector_cs: Evropský Spotřební sektor & Autoprůmysl (např. Volvo, BMW)
recommendations.reason_cs: Pokračující krize v Rudém moři prodlužuje dodavatelské řetězce a zvyšuje náklady na přepravu komponentů z Asie. To negativně doléhá na marže evropských výrobců a spotřebitelskou důvěru.
recommendations.reason_en: The ongoing Red Sea crisis extends supply chains and increases shipping costs for components from Asia. This negatively impacts the margins of European manufacturers and consumer confidence.

recommendations.sector_cs: Pražská burza: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.sector_en: Prague Stock Exchange: ČEZ, Komerční banka, Erste Group
recommendations.reason_cs: Domácí tituly jsou primárně ovlivněny evropskou makroekonomickou situací a domácí monetární politikou. Geopolitické napětí v Jemenu na ně má jen nepřímý a omezený vliv skrze globální náladu.
recommendations.reason_en: Domestic equities are primarily driven by the European macroeconomic environment and local monetary policy. Geopolitical tensions in Yemen have only an indirect and limited impact via global sentiment.

recommendations.sector_cs: Evropské blue-chips (např. Airbus, TotalEnergies, Allianz, Rheinmetall)
recommendations.sector_en: European blue-chips (e.g. Airbus, TotalEnergies, Allianz, Rheinmetall)
recommendations.reason_cs: Smíšený vliv eskalace na Blízkém východě; zatímco energetické a zbrojní tituly těží z růstu cen a poptávky, širší trh čelí zvýšené volatilitě a rizikům pro dodavatelské řetězce.
recommendations.reason_en: Mixed impact from the Middle East escalation; while energy and defense stocks benefit from higher prices and demand, the broader market faces increased volatility and supply chain risks.

assessment.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování rozsáhlé vládní ofenzívy v Jemenu podpořené nálety koalice, na což Hútíové odpoví dalšími asymetrickými útoky na saúdskou infrastrukturu. Napětí v oblasti Rudého moře a úžiny Bab al-Mandab zůstane na kritické úrovni.
assessment.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the large-scale government offensive in Yemen backed by coalition airstrikes is expected to continue, prompting the Houthis to respond with further asymmetric attacks on Saudi infrastructure. Tension in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab strait will remain at a critical level.
assessment.forecast_review_cs: Předchozí předpověď se plně potvrdila; intenzivní bojové operace a letecké údery v Jemenu pokračují a Hútíové stupňují odvetné útoky na saúdskou infrastrukturu.
assessment.forecast_review_en: The previous forecast was fully confirmed; intensive combat operations and airstrikes in Yemen are continuing, and the Houthis are stepping up retaliatory attacks on Saudi infrastructure.

articles.title: Argentina to stop Falklands exploiting offshore oilfields, country’s foreign minister says
articles.summary:
Pablo Quirno says move is part of government’s strategy to peacefully assert sovereignty over the islands

Argentina’s foreign minister has told an audience that included the British ambassador that his government would stop the Falkland Islands from exploiting its offshore oilfields as part of a strategy to take sovereignty.

During a speech at a thinktank event in the Argentinian capital, Pablo Quirno condemned the British government for failing to open negotiations over the islands and facilitating a significant offshore oil project in its waters.

articles.title: Keeping up with the Bolsonaros: Flávio’s surprise first-round election win heralds rise of a political dynasty
articles.summary:
Four members of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro’s family have been elected to office, most notably his wife and son Flávio, who won the first round of voting to be Brazil’s new president

The weekend’s elections in Brazil not only put Jair Bolsonaro’s eldest son, Flávio Bolsonaro, in the lead in the presidential race, but also underscored how far the former president has come in building a political dynasty.

As his far-right senator son heads into a runoff against the leftist incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a sweeping far-right victory in congressional races also secured seats for Jair Bolsonaro’s wife, two of his sons and one of his brothers.

articles.title: Fuel from South Korea being shipped to Russia as Ukraine war grinds on
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Guardian analysis finds more than 150,000 tonnes of fuel was shipped to Russian ports in July and August, some using sanctioned tankers

Fuel is being shipped from South Korea to Russia via sanctioned tankers as Moscow scrambles for supplies amid the war in Ukraine, a move one expert said “undermines” Seoul’s public backing for Kyiv.

Guardian analysis of port records and ship-tracking data found that in July and August over 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mostly diesel, was loaded at several South Korean ports on to seven tankers that made 14 voyages to Russia’s far east.

articles.title: Extreme heat warnings issued for parts of southern California
articles.summary:
Temperatures in US state forecast to hit high 30s celsius this week, while regions in Indonesia grapple with wildfires

The National Weather Service in the US has issued extreme heat warnings for parts of southern California, including Los Angeles, until Thursday, as temperatures are expected to hit the high 30s celsius. Burbank, a suburb north of Los Angeles, recorded 39C on Saturday, a few degrees shy of the October record for the region set in 1987. A persistent area of high pressure will remain in place this week, leading to further hazardous hot weather and increased fire risk.

Parts of Indonesia are in the midst of an extreme wildfire season, which has peaked over the past month. Western Kalimantan (Borneo) and southern Sumatra have been particularly badly affected. The lack of rainfall has dried the usually water-logged tropical soils, meaning that fires have been able to spread quickly, above and below the surface. Indonesia’s soils are also extremely rich in peat, meaning that the smoke produced from the fires contain higher levels of toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide. Cities in surrounding areas and as far as Malaysia and Singapore have experienced reduced air quality in recent weeks as a result. Drought and wildfires are more common in this part of the world during El Niño events owing to suppressed thunderstorm activity.

articles.title: Saudi-backed forces recapture key areas around strait from Houthis in Yemen
articles.summary:
Government offensive launched under air cover by Saudi military coalition aims to retake all Houthi-held territory

Forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen have recaptured several key areas around Bab al-Mandab strait from Iran-backed Houthi rebels, Yemeni officials said on Monday.

The officials said forces allied with the internationally recognized government have retaken the crucial town of Dhubab just north of the strait. They also captured the towns of Bab and Hadeid, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. Witnesses said they saw government tanks and forces entering the towns.

articles.title: Houthis say Saudi airports, Aramco facilities being targeted
articles.summary:
Houthis say Saudi airports, Aramco facilities being targeted

Yemen’s Houthis on Monday said the group is actively targeting airports and Saudi Aramco oil facilities in Saudi Arabia with drones and ballistic missiles, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said.

He described the attacks as retaliation for the Saudi blockade and recent air strikes on Yemen, including the capital, Sanaa.

Saudi officials said fighter jets carried out hundreds of air strikes on Yemen on Monday as the internationally recognised government launched a ground offensive aimed at retaking areas lost to the Houthis in southwestern Yemen and along the Red Sea coast. 

The intensified Saudi strikes have been followed by an increase in Houthi missile and drone attacks on the kingdom.

articles.title: Ethiopia pushes to secure Red Sea access as Tigray war raises regional tensions
articles.summary:
Ethiopia pushes to secure Red Sea access as Tigray war raises regional tensions

Submitted by MEE staff on Tue, 10/06/2026 - 12:01
Addis Ababa says its ‘legitimate interests’ in the Red Sea must be recognised as Eritrea, Sudan and other neighbours reject unilateral moves
A general view of Berbera Port and the city of Berbera, Somaliland, 31 August 2021 (Ed Ram/AFP)
Off

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has renewed his call for access to the Red Sea, saying his landlocked country will work to secure an outlet to the sea as fighting in the north threatens to deepen tensions with its neighbours.

Abiy made the remarks on Monday as he was sworn in for another five-year term, with Ethiopian government forces having retaken Mekele, the capital of the Tigray region, after a renewed offensive by an opposition alliance led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front.

“Based on the principle of give and take, we will work diligently to ensure that Ethiopia has an outlet to the sea,” he said. 

Since neighbouring Eritrea gained independence in 1993, Ethiopia has been landlocked, as the newly created state took away the port of Assab and with it Ethiopia's access to the sea.

Earlier this year, a former Ethiopian government adviser told Middle East Eye that Ethiopia's key ally, the United Arab Emirates, was "calling the shots" in regard to Eritrea and any Ethiopian plans to retake Assab by force.

Since 1993, Ethiopia has relied on the port of Djibouti for sea access, but it has long sought alternative arrangements.

In January 2024, Ethiopia signed a memorandum of understanding with Somaliland, the breakaway region of Somalia also backed by the UAE and recognised by Israel, that envisaged access to the sea and a potential naval presence. 

Inside Somaliland: How Berbera Port is central to the Red Sea's power struggle
Read More »

Somalia condemned the agreement as a violation of its sovereignty, although relations between Addis Ababa and Mogadishu subsequently improved.

Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud said the country did not object to Ethiopia gaining access to the sea through Somali territory. 

“I look forward to working closely together to strengthen Somalia-Ethiopia relations & advance peace, stability & shared prosperity for our peoples & the Horn of Africa,” Mohamud said in a post congratulating Abiy on his new term.

Ethiopia's other neighbours have taken a harder line.

On Sunday, the leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia met in Egypt's New Alamein and issued a joint declaration affirming “the principle of freedom of navigation”, while saying that “the governance of the Red Sea is the exclusive responsibility of the littoral states”.

The declaration also called for respect for international law governing transboundary rivers, including the Nile, and rejected unilateral measures affecting the existing water uses of Egypt and Sudan.

In April, MEE revealed that an Ethiopian army base was being used to support the UAE-backed Rapid Support Forces in the Sudan war.

Dispute over maritime access   

Ethiopia’s push for Red Sea access has become a growing source of tension with its neighbours.

While Addis Ababa sees this as necessary to ensure the country’s economic and geopolitical security, Eritrea, Egypt, Sudan, and Somalia have stressed that coastal states have jurisdiction over their territorial waters.

Exclusive: The Ethiopian army base covertly supporting Sudan’s RSF
Read More »

Somalia has opened the possibility of granting Ethiopia conditional access to the sea, if the two countries reach a formal agreement. 

The dispute comes as fighting has intensified in Ethiopia’s northern Tigray region, with government-aligned forces retaking the regional capital Mekele after renewed clashes with Tigrayan forces.

The escalation has raised fears of the conflict spiralling into a larger regional confrontation. 

Eritrea finds itself in the middle of the discord, as Ethiopia has long sought to gain access to the Red Sea through Eritrean ports.

The two neighbouring states have had a hostile relationship for decades, with Eritrea cutting diplomatic ties with Ethiopia last week after Addis Ababa closed its embassy in Asmara and expelled ten Eritrean diplomats.

This deterioration in relations comes on the heels of the two countries’ dispute with Egypt and Sudan over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, which threatens to divert water from the Nile.

The African Union has called for restraint and dialogue as hostilities in northern Ethiopia intensify, urging the parties to seek a peaceful resolution to the crisis.

articles.title: France pledges $3.36m in assistance to Yemen
articles.summary:
France pledges $3.36m in assistance to Yemen

France has pledged an additional $3.36m to Yemen as renewed fighting displaces more than 200,000 people.

“The Houthi offensive in the ‌Bab al-Mandab strait has triggered a new humanitarian shock,” French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told humanitarian groups in Paris.

“In response to ⁠this tragedy, I ⁠have decided to allocate an additional 3m euros in support, bringing ⁠our total aid to the Yemeni population ⁠to more than ⁠7m euros in 2026."

articles.title: Houthis say they targeted Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport with missiles
articles.summary:
Houthis say they targeted Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport with missiles

Yemen's Houthis said they targeted Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport in the south-west of the country with missiles on Tuesday.

"We reiterate our warning to all international airlines regarding the consequences of continuing to operate flights within Saudi airspace, as it has become a theatre for our military operations - with the exception of the airspace over the Holy Sites in Mecca and Medina," the group said in a statement.

The Saudi government has yet to confirm the attack.
